kind: v31 retune: base-ratio saturation re-split, wrap retraction, cap==policy, mixed-digest key, literal sweep

saturation.statement: distinct base ratios <= min(nb^2, 2^98); the recoverable set is mu6*(A/B)*(W/W) of size <= 6*min(nb^2,2^98)*ell^2

v30.verdict: reviewer's bound reproduces: 6*nb^2*ell^2/m = 2^-34.97, not 0.51 -- the v30 success claim is void at production (fixture never saturated)

v31.note: min(nb^2,2^98)=nb^2 so the reviewer's own form equals 6N^2/m = K: no clip

birthday.law: distinct differences of a random nb-subset of a G-element group = G(1-e^{-nb^2/G})
birthday.why: the verdict's nb=2^48 sits AT x=1/4: 11.5% of the ratio set is lost to difference collisions, q falls to ~0.351 and the 0.39 floor fails. v31 takes nb=2^45 (x=1/256, 0.19% loss) -- the saturation fix must be 3 bits tighter than the bare nb^2<=2^98
birthday.calibration: fixture nb=181 span=16 x=0.25 predicts 0.396*0.885=0.3504, measured 0.351750 (0.4% agreement) -- the attenuator is measured, not assumed

gap.policy: ABORT AT FIRST ABOVE-CAP GAP (the implemented behaviour; v30 claimed a 4-fallback schedule its code never ran). (a) each base's even-gap table is built to at most K_max/2 = 2^31 entries, a DETERMINISTIC function of the cap; (b) a realised gap above K_max aborts the trail, which then contributes no success and its work is charged; (c) there is NO fallback row: K_max is chosen so that no trail is expected to abort
gap.band_note: walk band = ell*mu is DERIVED from the retuned ell (v30's 2^76 was the same derivation at ell=2^49.65); at ell=2^70.65 it is 2^96.72
gap.why_K_max_moved: v30's K_max=2^31 does NOT survive the retune: lam = ell*e^{-K/mu} is ell/ell30 = 2^21.00 larger at the same cap, so 2^31 would abort every trail (lam=2^26.58). 2^32 restores lam=2^-17.50.

three_way.census_source: arm-retune-v31.jsonl (the run that produced the charged q)

cap_demo.note: at the fixture's own p99 trail-max gap the cap FIRES (v30 measured 3.85% aborts against 65.2% predicted by the unsuppressed law), so the abort counter is an exercised code path, not a story; at the policy cap the census above fires 0/24000 and the Poisson upper bound on the abort rate is 1.248e-04

wrap.v30_claim_retracted: v30 asserted 'span+walk_band<41 => a_i*w_k is an exact integer product, wrap_free'. RETRACTED: the code computes mulmod(a,W[k]), a field multiplication that reduces mod p by definition; no bound on integer representatives is needed and none was established
wrap.object_claimed: record = a_i * W_k mod p, a_i = GH^{k_i} (k_i < 2^97 pool exponent), W_k a distinct H-element; the arithmetic is the group law, which is exact mod p for every input pair

wrap_probability.definition: integer-level wrap = the product of the two representatives is >= p, so the stored residue is the reduced one
wrap_probability.verdict: the integer product wraps with probability >= 1-2^-20 at the fixture and >= 1-2^-96.7 at production: O(1) wrap, by design. v31 makes NO no-wrap claim. The only exponent-domain statement that IS used is the base-difference count (2^98 capacity), which is a count, not a no-wrap assumption

wrap.key_domain_note: the key is a mixed digest of the FULL residue (168-bit truncation of a 2-round xorshift-multiply finaliser), so it does not read the low-bit structure that the v30 low-bit key exposed; measured side by side below

retuned_shape.role: PRODUCTION-SHAPE ARM: the retuned split (nb^2/2^98 = 2^-8, K held at 6N^2/m), the production base law (g^k), the mixed key, the policy cap
retuned_shape.abort_census: 0 aborts in 24000 trials at the policy cap; one-sided Poisson 95% upper bound on the abort rate = 2.996/24000 = 1.248e-04
retuned_shape.shape_note: the production split ratio nb/ell cannot be reproduced at fixture N (it needs nb<1); what IS reproduced is the saturation ratio nb^2/space, which is the quantity flaw 1 is about

saturation_control.role: PLANTED CONTROL: same N, same K, same span count -- only nb^2/space is broken
saturation_control.verdict: q collapses from 0.39-class to 0.0155 when nb^2/space = 32: the reviewer's mechanism is REPRODUCIBLE at fixture scale, and it is the only knob that moves q here

crown_banked.role: BANKED measured fixture evidence (reviewer-accepted v30 crown)
crown_banked.rung: nb=22, ell=6944 (108.5x the fixture walk length)

arms.ladder_note: the crown rung (nb=22, ell=6944, nb^2/space=2^-8.1) is the same saturation shape as the retuned production split; it stays banked and unchanged

kappa.key_rule: key = truncate(mix64(residue), KEY_BITS) with mix64 = 2-round xorshift-multiply (fmix64 shape); v30 truncated the raw residue, whose low bits carry the stride structure of the walk -- the reviewer's clustering objection
kappa.paired_design: ONE walk set, TWO stores: the low-bit key and the mixed key are counted on the same walks, so the difference is not a sampling difference

clustering_diag.verdict: the low-bit key's max exceeds the mixed key's by 1.9312 (132.4% of the charged value): the clustering objection is REAL but SMALL at this truncation, and the mixed key is the one charged, so the charge is not understated by it

row_derivation.records: 2*rps*2242: rps=nb*ell records/side x 2242 charged instructions (201 itemised + 242 charged overhead at 1.2x; +4 over v30's 2238 = the mixed-digest finaliser)
row_derivation.base_entry_nw50: 2*nb*121*2000: 121 instructions/base to form the record-window entry, both sides
row_derivation.gap_point_tables: 2*nb*(K_max/2)*15*2000: <=K_max/2 even-gap entries/base (DETERMINISTIC cap), 15 per table point
row_derivation.walker_state_nw50: 2*nb*4: one 1-word walk cursor per base per side, 4 instructions
row_derivation.gap_tail_fallback: 0: the abort-at-first policy serves NO fallback (v30 charged a 4-call schedule its code never ran)
row_derivation.chain_tables: carried v26 declared integer: chain-table entries x build rate, counted at the v26 nb=N sizing
row_derivation.fixed_per_node: carried: per-node fixed setup x node count
row_derivation.hprime_supply: carried: H-prime sieving supply for the walk list
row_derivation.run_pair_cap: carried: 2^95 run pairs x 2 instructions / unit
row_derivation.walk_list: carried: walk-list build rate x list length, counted at the v26 sizing
row_derivation.gap_self_check: carried: self-check pass over the drawn bands

ledger.integer_assert: total == sum(rows); every row a Python int; regenerated from rows

carried_row_census.note: every carried row's count is a function of at most the v26 base count (nb=N) or the walk-list length; v31's nb=2^45 and ell=2^70.65 are both below the v26 sizing, so the carried integers are an upper bound. They are 0.0147% of W: doubling ALL of them moves W by 0.000212 bits

applicability: nw=2^50 geometry: nb=2^45 bases/side, ell=2^70.65 steps
